From the 10-K Item 7 passage the desk returned, the company says future results, including debt levels, could differ materially because of “global or regional changes or imbalances in the supply and demand for oil, natural gas, petrochemicals, and feedstocks” and “changes in interest and exchange rates,” and it also says the company faces “the ability to access debt markets on favorable terms or at all.” The desk did not return a quantified debt-maturity schedule or a quantified floating-rate note from the filing text, so I cannot state a maturity ladder or floating-rate percentage from what was provided. What I can say is that the filing language itself flags both commodity and rate sensitivity as live risks.

For the book, XOM is only 4.61% as of 2026-09-10, up 0.01% from 4.60% on 2026-09-09, so this is a modest position rather than a dominant one. The portfolio’s beta to SPY is -0.56× over 1y, which tells you the book is not being run as a broad equity market beta book; it has a defensive or offsetting mix. I could not get a beta to USO from the desk, so I cannot quantify the book’s oil beta directly. Given that limit, the practical reading is: if oil falls, XOM’s own leverage and cash-coverage headroom are still solid, but they are less forgiving than a year ago, so the position would be more vulnerable to a sustained commodity shock than the 2025 quarter set implied. If you want, I can next pull XOM’s price.beta versus SPY and its price reaction to oil-linked moves, then tie that to the 4.61% weight more tightly."}

The desk says JPMorgan’s market risk readout is mixed, but not obviously “riskier than a year ago” on the measures it can show directly.

- Operating cash flow has also strengthened, from $1.47B on 2024-06-30 to $5.33B on 2026-03-31.
